title: Nat.lpo_implies_wlpo: the limited principle of omniscience yields its weak form
statement: Written over a Bool-valued sequence f : Nat -> Bool, which is Bishop's formulation: Hits f := exists n, f n = true ("f fires somewhere") and Misses f := forall n, f n = false ("f never fires"). LPO is forall f, Or (Hits f) (Misses f); WLPO is forall f, Or (Misses f) (Not (Misses f)); Markov's principle (MP) is forall f, Not (Misses f) -> Hits f; LLPO is forall f g, Not (And (Hits f) (Hits g)) -> Or (Misses f) (Misses g); EM is forall (P : Prop), Or P (Not P). LPO returns a WITNESS when the sequence fires; WLPO returns only a DECISION about whether it never fires. This edge is the forgetful direction, and it is the cheap one: the Hits branch refutes Misses pointwise at the witness through Bool.false_ne_true. The interesting content is that the converse is NOT this edge reversed -- see F:nat-wlpo-and-markov-imply-lpo, where recovering LPO from WLPO needs Markov's principle as a second hypothesis. THE PRINCIPLE IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT AN AXIOM. It is spelled out inline in the type -- never behind a Definition -- so a reader of the rendered statement sees the whole assumption and nothing about the conclusion can be smuggled into an abbreviation. That is why axiom_footprint is empty. ADR-1601 (roadmap W0-2) decides this policy and prices it: across the ten theorems of this family the hypothesis route costs 11 binders and 14 argument positions and ZERO proof obligations. WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not claim the principle in its hypothesis is true, false, or independent. The SEPARATIONS in the standard picture -- LPO is not constructively derivable, LLPO does not give LPO, WLPO does not give LPO, MP does not give WLPO -- are CITED here (Bishop, Constructive Analysis ch. 1) and are not proved: each needs a model of this kernel rather than a term in it, and ADR-1600 records why an internal metatheorem about this kernel is unavailable.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.lpo_implies_wlpo : ((x0 : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> Or (Exists.{1} AxNat (fun (x1 : AxNat) => Eq.{1} Bool (x0 x1) Bool.true)) (((x1 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Bool (x0 x1) Bool.false)))) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> Or (((x2 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Bool (x1 x2) Bool.false)) (Not (((x2 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Bool (x1 x2) Bool.false)))))

evidence.supports: Nat.lpo_implies_wlpo is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example kernel_declaration_projection -- --require-declaration Nat.lpo_implies_wlpo --require-kind theorem
evidence.notes: --require-declaration exits non-zero when the name is absent from every constructed prelude, and --require-kind exits non-zero when it is present with the wrong kind, so the exit status depends on the finding rather than on the run completing. --release is MANDATORY: this binary builds creal/complex/cpoint, which overflow the default debug thread stack.

evidence.notes: The suite's own footprint test reads Kernel::axiom_footprint for every declaration in the family and fails on a non-empty result. The grep -c count is what makes the command discriminating: a fabricated or renamed filter makes cargo print a different passed-count and exit 0, and the anchored pattern then matches nothing, so grep -c prints 0 and exits 1. grep -c rather than grep -q, which would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail. Anchored with [[:space:]]-free literals, never \t -- in a scripted (GNU) grep \t is a literal t.

evidence.supports: The statement is the one advertised, not a weaker or stronger one: the theorem is applied at GENUINELY FREE variables of the hypothesis type and the inferred conclusion is pinned against an independently rebuilt term, and a negative control in the hypothesis slot is REQUIRED TO BE REJECTED.
evidence.checker_command: cargo test -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib lpo_implies_wlpo_lands_on_the_decision_and_rejects_wlpo_in_its_own_slot -- --test-threads=4 2>&1 | grep -cE '^test result: ok\. 1 passed'
evidence.notes: Numerals reduce and hide definitional-equality gaps, so nothing in this test instantiates a sequence or a real concretely. The builders in the test file are a SECOND, independent implementation of every principle: if they called the module's own private helpers, the check would be comparing a term with itself and could not fail.

notes: The negative control is the one that carries the weight: WLPO itself must NOT discharge LPO's hypothesis slot. The two types differ in ONE subterm -- `Hits f` against `Misses f` in the left disjunct -- which is exactly the distinction the whole map turns on.
